data_supported_interpretations.statement: Endpoint 0 is not the source of the apparent bowl/tray offset: both saved actual conditions match the kinematic reference to numerical precision at endpoint 0. The first material relative-configuration review interval is 15-17, where target-frame tool/target translation error rises from 17.46 mm at endpoint 15 to 25.37 mm at endpoint 16 and the first recorded right-index/tool contact appears at 16 then disappears at 17.

The visible disagreement after endpoint 23 is accumulated tracking divergence rather than a rendered teleport. The trajectories and saved substeps evolve continuously; FROZEN_SUFFIX_BASELINE and OVERLAP_PLAN begin to separate after the declared overlap boundary.

OVERLAP_PLAN reduces late target/tray absolute error relative to FROZEN_SUFFIX_BASELINE, but it does not uniformly improve bowl pose or bowl/tray relative pose. At endpoint 60 the saved legacy scores remain below 1 (0.9518 candidate, 0.9889 baseline), which is neutral legacy-tracking evidence and not a visual task-success certification.

left_hand_target.statement: No unequivocal left-hand/tray geometric failure is visible in 0-24. The first clearly growing reference-vs-actual tray separation is 25-27, coincident with the largest early target-position increments. This is a review interval, not a failure declaration.

right_hand_tool.statement: The first recorded right-index/tool contact appears at endpoint 16 and disappears at 17 while tool rotation error rises. The images remain physically continuous, so this is a contact/motion turning point rather than proof of a bad grasp.

tool_target.statement: The first material saved tool/target relative-pose change occurs across 15-17. Endpoint 0 is aligned and 0-14 shows only gradual millimetre-scale drift; no abrupt initial bowl/tray relocation is visible.

hypotheses.statement: The 15-17 transition may be where early contact timing begins to seed the later bowl/tray relative-pose divergence. The current visual package does not establish causality.

The user's apparent early bowl/tray mismatch may partly reflect comparing an independent RGB camera with fixed simulator top/oblique cameras. Camera calibration or independent 3-D object pose evidence is required before treating cross-column pixel displacement as a physical mismatch.

limitations: REAL RGB is time-aligned but uses an independent, uncalibrated camera; it is not pixel-registered to either simulator view.
Endpoint images and sheets cannot prove fingertip contact under occlusion. Semantic contact transitions come from saved contact records and remain navigation evidence.
Substep RGB uses the nearest real frame and the kinematic reference is held at an endpoint; both limitations are labelled in every substep image.
Saved contact force is reported numerically, but no force vector is drawn because solve-time geometry correspondence was not independently established.
The review covers only saved endpoints 0-60 and the predeclared saved-substep windows; it does not authorize or infer behavior outside that range.
next_minimum_evidence: For a stronger claim about the apparent early bowl/tray mismatch, obtain calibrated RGB camera extrinsics or an independent synchronized 3-D pose check for endpoints 15-17. For contact causality, preserve solve-time contact geometry aligned to the saved wrench. Neither requires rerunning this visual package.

observations.statement: All 61 endpoints were reviewed in both fixed views using all 14 contact sheets; early, middle, and late full-resolution frames and six saved-substep comparisons were opened separately.
At endpoint 0, ROBOT REFERENCE, FROZEN_SUFFIX_BASELINE, and OVERLAP_PLAN are visually coincident; saved tool, target, and world-pair translation errors are at numerical-noise scale.

Across endpoints 0-14, the simulated tray remains left of the bowl and both hands retain the expected object roles. No discontinuous relocation, floor penetration, or object explosion is visible in either fixed view.

Endpoints 15-20 show a continuous but more dynamic hand/object transition. At endpoint 16 the saved target-frame tool/target translation error is 25.37 mm and right-index/tool contact appears; the contact disappears at endpoint 17.
Between endpoints 23-32, actual/reference separation grows smoothly and the two actual conditions start to diverge. No frame-to-frame teleport is visible in endpoint or saved-substep panels.

Between endpoints 43-60, bowl tracking and bowl/tray relative-pose disagreement become visually obvious. OVERLAP_PLAN generally keeps the tray closer to reference late in the window, while its bowl rotation error is not uniformly better.
